newsitem.title: UK: UK 1995 govt deficit revised to 5.6 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: UK 1995 govt deficit revised to 5.6 pct of GDP.

text.p: The UK general government financial deficit was 5.6 of GDP in 1995, revised down from the previous estimate of 5.8 percent, the Office for National Statistics said on Friday.
This compares with a ratio of 6.8 percent in 1994 and 7.8 percent in 1993.
In the fiscal year 1995-96, the deficit was revised to 5.0 percent of GDP from 5.1 percent at the previous estimate.
General government gross debt in 1995 was 54.1 percent of GDP, unchanged from the previous estimate. This compares with 50.5 in 1994 and 48.5 percent in 1993.
In the fiscal year 1995-96, the gross debt ratio was 53.8 percent of GDP, also unchanged since the last estimate.
These estimates are made under the terms of the Maastricht Treaty which requires member states to avoid excessive government deficits and report planned and actual deficits and debt levels to the EC.
Protocol to the Treaty states a reference value of 3.0 percent of GDP for financial deficits and 60 percent of GDP for debt.
First estimates for calendar 1996 deficit and debt levels will be released on Thursday, March 27, the ONS said.
